final.investment_thesis:
Direction and size. The risk debate did not produce a genuine conflict on direction: the Aggressive, Conservative and Neutral seats all recommended a 3.0% total target, the Research Manager recommended Underweight and 3%, and the Trader proposed Sell with the same 3% sizing. The only live disagreements are (a) what the 3% is *for* — optionality, a risk limit, or a 'watching brief' — and (b) whether the residual should be zero. I resolve that in favour of the Conservative/Neutral framing of the position as a risk limit, but reject the Conservative implication that a risk-limit position carries no economic upside, and I reject a 0% liquidation outright. Rating stays Underweight because this is a partial de-risking of an intact franchise, not an exit; the executable target, not the label, does the work.

Why reduce at all — the decisive evidence. The 2026-07-31 shock is the gate: a -8.58% session on 2.6x volume that opened a 310.69–333.43 gap which is still completely unfilled, i.e. real supply overhead rather than momentum decay in place. Price at 312.41 sits below the 10-EMA (317.58), the VWMA (320.95) and the Bollinger mid (323.53), and the Aug 5 positive catalysts failed to reclaim the 10-EMA. The bounce off the 302.56 low came on falling volume (75.1M → 46.1M), which is the absence of institutional sponsorship, and the MACD histogram (-3.48) with RSI 46.9 shows momentum un-repaired. Layered on that is the bear's corrected margin arithmetic, which the bull never neutralized: at roughly 34x peak-cycle EPS on a peak ~50% gross margin, a reset to 48% gross margin is about $9B of annualized gross profit — some 5–6% of pre-tax income, not the $2.2B/2% the bull used — so forward memory-cost guidance is a multiple-compression risk. Nothing in the six prior AAPL Underweights that bled 3–8% of alpha applies cleanly here: those trimmed intact stacked uptrends on momentum decay alone, whereas this one is anchored to a printed volume-distribution event and a price below every short-term average. That same history is why I will not go below 3%.

Why not zero (the lower allocation). 0% is mechanically trivial — $99,921.57 of equity is 94% cash and selling another $3,000 costs ~$3 in fees — but it is not justified on evidence. The primary trend is intact: the 200-SMA at 279.16 is rising and spot is 11.9% above it, the 50-SMA at 309.74 has held on a closing basis, nine-month FCF is +52.5%, and the balance sheet is a fortress. Liquidating would pay a fee to forfeit the convexity of a volume-confirmed reclaim of 317.58 or a 305–307 flush-and-reverse, and the AMZN/GOOGL lessons of the past week both cut the same way: when the debate is genuinely two-sided, let the two-sidedness cap the trim rather than justify maximal de-risking. The position is also essentially at cost (average cost including fees 309.89 versus 312.41, unrealized +$48.82), so there is no tax or loss-harvesting argument for forcing an exit.

Why not 6% or 10% (the higher allocations). Holding the current 6.06% keeps full exposure to the unfilled 310.69–333.43 gap and to the margin-reset risk before any confirmed reclaim, and it does so while price is below the 10-EMA, VWMA and Bollinger mid — that is not a risk I am paid to carry at 34x peak EPS. A 10% target would be outright counter-trend adding into a decaying-volume bounce, which no analyst proposed and the evidence does not support.

Downside versus cash opportunity cost, both weighed honestly. On the downside, a further 20% drawdown to ~250 costs about 0.6% of total equity at a 3% weight — roughly $600 — versus about 1.2% at the current 6.06%; against a 94% cash balance that is tolerable but not free, which is precisely why some trim is warranted. On the other side, cash earns no interest and already carries most of the bull-case opportunity cost: if AAPL gapped toward the 333–344 gap-fill zone the 3% retained position contributes roughly +0.2% to +0.3% of account return, and if it ran toward ~380 (+21.6%) the ~0.65% of account return given up by trimming from 6% to 3% is the explicit price of the de-risking. I judge that price acceptable because the reward/risk at spot is only about 1.7:1 to first resistance, entry triggers are better defined (305–307 flush, or a confirmed reclaim above 317.58 on >65M shares), and neither risk avoidance nor cash opportunity cost dominates the other at these sizes.

Why 3% is a real position and not an 'observation post'. Observing evidence does not require holding stock, so I am not defending the residual on observation grounds. At $99,921.57 of equity, 3% is ~$2,998 — small, but its economic purpose is defined and asymmetric: it preserves participation in a franchise whose balance sheet, FCF and rising 200-SMA remain constructive, and it provides convexity into the Q4 print and a possible gap fill, at a worst-case cost near 0.6% of equity. That purpose is preferable to zero after fees because the fee to liquidate (~$3) buys nothing, while the exposure retains optionality into two specific, named catalysts. Equally, I impose no minimum: if the 300 level broke on heavy volume or Q4 gross margin came in below 48% with memory costs left unquantified, 0% would be the correct target and I would take it.

Disagreement resolved. The Aggressive seat is right that the trend and FCF make a full exit wrong, but wrong to make 'breakout optionality' the *primary* reason for holding — before the VWMA and gap are reclaimed, the position is a risk limit first. The Conservative is right on that point but overreaches in implying the residual has no economic value and in wanting a mechanical zero on a 300 break; I keep the 300/heavy-volume condition as a reassessment trigger rather than an automatic liquidation. The Neutral's convexity framing, the AMZN/GOOGL 'let two-sidedness cap the trim' lesson and the 2026-07-30 'gate an Underweight on an actual distribution print, not momentum decay' lesson together produce exactly 3.0% — a halving, sized independently of yesterday's holding.

What would change the call. Upgrade toward Overweight on a daily close above 317.58 on >65M shares, or a 305–307 flush that reverses with volume, since those confirm the 50-SMA/200-SMA structure is being defended; a volume-confirmed reclaim of the 333.43 gap edge would justify rebuilding materially. Move to 0% on a heavy-volume daily close below 300, or if Q4 gross margin falls below 48% with the memory-cost impact left unquantified. Missing and stated rather than papered over: no product-level revenue or segment mix, insider transactions and pre-Aug-5 news coverage unavailable (only 20 of 213 records supplied), no verified valuation multiple or consensus series, and no explicit entry price — hence confidence is low and no valuation-derived price target is issued.
final.time_horizon: 1-3 months tactical, re-underwritten at the Q4 FY2026 print and on any volume-confirmed reclaim of 317.58
